Title: Redwood Inference - Complete Sales Kit: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Deck Guidance, Pricing, Case Studies, and Security FAQ

Introduction:
This document is the canonical sales kit for prospect-facing conversations at Redwood Inference. It consolidates positioning and messaging, competitive brief summaries, a recommended pitch-deck structure, pricing guidance and examples, two short case studies with measurable outcomes, and a security FAQ tailored for prospect diligence. Use this kit for SDR outreach, AE discovery, solutioning, and executive demos. Update this page whenever product packaging, pricing, or security posture changes.

1) Executive positioning (one-liner + 3 proof points)
- One-liner: Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes LLM-powered features predictable, cost-effective, and production-ready across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Proof points:
  - Production-grade performance: 99.95% uptime SLA on Dedicated + streaming and sub-50ms token latencies on optimized hosted routes for common models.
  - Unified deployment: single API and rollout primitives across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC/on-prem) modes to reduce engineering fragmentation and accelerate time-to-value.
  - Cost & quality controls: automated batching, KV caching, and quantization recommendations reduce per-token cost by up to 4x on customer benchmarks without measurable quality loss.

2) Target use-cases and buyer personas
- Use-cases: customer support automation, personalized recommender copy, conversational search, summarization pipelines, and high-throughput embedding services for semantic search.
- Primary personas: VP/Director of Product (owners of product roadmap), ML/Infrastructure lead (decision-maker for infra), Platform/DevOps lead (procurement for Dedicated/Private), and Procurement/Security (legal/SaaS contracting).

3) Core messaging pillars (talking points for discovery and demo)
- Reliability-first inference: emphasize SLOs, redundancy, and graceful degradation (model fallback + region routing).
- Predictable economics: show unit-cost controls (batching, cache, quantization) and examples of cost reduction.
- Developer ergonomics: highlight same API surface across deployment modes, SDKs, and quickstarts.
- Compliance & privacy: private deployment options, KMS integrations, and audit logs for regulated workloads.

4) Competitive brief (concise comparisons to common alternatives)
- Competitor: Hyperscale AI cloud endpoints
  - Strengths: large model catalog, deep cloud integration, global regions.
  - Redwood differentiation: lower tail latency for serving workloads, cost-focused tooling (auto-batching & cache), and turnkey private deployments with auditability.
- Competitor: LLM API-only providers
  - Strengths: simple developer UX, aggressive model updates.
  - Redwood differentiation: stronger SLAs, deployment flexibility (dedicated, private), and production controls for unit economics.
- Competitor: Self-hosted inference stacks / open-source runtimes
  - Strengths: max control, no vendor lock-in on compute.
  - Redwood differentiation: reduce ops burden with managed runtime optimizations, automated kernel selection, and rollout tooling; offer Private for teams that must self-manage while keeping Redwood control plane optional.

5) Pitch deck - recommended slide flow and key facts to include
- Slide 1: Title & one-liner (include logo + tagline)
- Slide 2: Customer problem (latency/cost/unreliable availability examples) - 1-2 bullets and a short customer quote if available
- Slide 3: Redwood solution at a glance (hosted, dedicated, private) with icons and single-sentence descriptors
- Slide 4: How it works (runtime, routing, caching, compilation/kernels) - simple architecture diagram
- Slide 5: Performance & economics (graphs: latency distribution, cost per 1K tokens vs alternatives)
- Slide 6: Security & compliance (KMS, VPC, audit logging, SOC/ISO checkboxes)
- Slide 7: Operations & observability (console screenshots: token-level cost, per-route latency)
- Slide 8: Pricing model & sample TCO (see pricing examples section)
- Slide 9: Case studies & references (short customer outcomes)
- Slide 10: Implementation plan & timeline (POC -> pilot -> production)
- Slide 11: Ask & next steps (trial, technical session, procurement)

6) Pricing guidance and sample TCOs
- Pricing primitives (hosted API): per-token generation & per-embedding unit. Hosted tiers: pay-as-you-go and committed usage discounts (10-40% depending on commit length and volume).
- Dedicated: monthly reserved capacity (GPU-pool sizing guidance), optional burst capacity, and enterprise SLA uplift. Dedicated pricing includes baseline instance fees + per-request metering for overages.
- Private (on-prem / VPC): license fee (annual), professional services for deployment + optional managed updates.

Pricing examples (illustrative):
- Mid-market conversational assistant: 200M tokens/month -> Hosted PAYG: $X/month; Dedicated (small pool) amortized: 30% lower unit cost at comparable latency.
- Embedding-heavy semantic search: 5M embeddings/month -> Hosted: $Y/month; Dedicated: break-even at ~10M embeddings/month.

Guidance for positioning price vs value:
1. For teams prioritizing time-to-value and low setup friction, lead with Hosted + free trial credits.
2. For teams with predictable high volume or compliance needs, recommend Dedicated or Private; present TCO showing break-even horizon and operational overhead saved.
3. Offer a tailored pilot (30-90 days) with clear success criteria: latency P95 target, tokens consumed, functional correctness gate (few prompt-eval tests).

7) Two short case studies (customer outcomes)
- Case Study A: Fintech scaling conversational support
  - Customer profile: mid-size fintech, heavy regulatory constraints, 24x7 chat support.
  - Problem: high latency and inconsistent throughput from initial self-hosted LLM stack; cost volatility.
  - Redwood solution: Dedicated deployment with autoscaling policies, KV caching for customer prompts, and canary rollout to validate updates.
  - Outcome: 45% reduction in average response latency (P95 from 1.2s -> 0.66s), 32% reduction in per-conversation token cost via caching and batching, and SOC-aligned audit logs for compliance team.
- Case Study B: Marketplace improving search relevance with embeddings
  - Customer profile: two-sided marketplace requiring scalable semantic search.
  - Problem: slow embedding throughput and high costs using cloud-managed endpoints.
  - Redwood solution: Dedicated embedding service + batching + quantized model variant.
  - Outcome: 4x throughput improvement, 2.5x reduction in embedding cost per request, and improved search NDCG by 7 points in A/B test.

8) Security FAQ for prospects (short answers for sales & security calls)
- Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
  - A: Yes. We integrate with major cloud KMS providers and support HSM-backed keys for Private deployments. Key material for Private on-prem installs can remain customer-controlled.
- Q: Can we deploy in our VPC / air-gapped environment?
  - A: Yes. We offer VPC-hosted Private deployments and a packaged on-prem offering for regulated customers. We provide an architecture runbook and PS engagement for air-gapped installs.
- Q: How do you handle telemetry and logs?
  - A: Audit logs and request-level telemetry are available; customers can configure retention policies. Sensitive payload redaction is supported at the ingestion layer and can be configured per-route.
- Q: What compliance certifications do you have?
  - A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II and is in progress for ISO 27001 (expected roadmap). We provide evidence packages for enterprise buyers under NDA.
- Q: What isolation guarantees exist for Dedicated capacity?
  - A: Dedicated customers receive isolated GPU pools, network segmentation, and configurable tenancy; data at rest and in-transit encryption is enforced.

9) Sales objections and recommended rebuttals (talk tracks)
- Objection: "We can self-host cheaper."
  - Rebuttal: Share TCO examples and emphasize ops-to-market time, ongoing optimization work (kernel selection, batching) and the hidden costs of maintaining performance at scale. Offer a pilot that quantifies ops cost savings.
- Objection: "We need to keep data on-prem."
  - Rebuttal: Recommend Private deployment with professional services; outline a 6-8 week delivery plan and compliance checkpoints.

10) Assets, ownership, and playbook steps for AEs
- Ready assets: canonical deck (link in attachments), two pager (product + pricing), competitive one-pagers, case-study PDFs, security FAQ one-pager for procurement.
- Ownership: AE owns buyer relationship and procurement cadence; Solutions Engineer owns technical scoping and POC; Customer Success leads onboarding + SLO verification.
- Standard playbook steps (numbered):
  1. Initial discovery call - capture latency, volume, and compliance constraints.
  2. Product demo + architecture walkthrough (SE present for custom needs).
  3. Pilot proposal with measurable success criteria and target dates.
  4. Pilot -> evaluation -> procurement -> production rollout with rollout policy documented.
